## Release privacy blocker

The full reachable commit-identity inventory contains a legacy personal-domain identity. This predates the current package change, but it prevents the repository from satisfying the no-personal-data history gate for future publication approval.

Required remediation:

- obtain explicit maintainer approval for a coordinated history rewrite
- inventory every branch and tag before mutation
- replace only the disallowed identity metadata
- preserve tags, releases, package provenance, and documented clone recovery
- independently verify all rewritten refs before publication is enabled

No history rewrite or publication is authorized by this issue.

PM item: [pm-context-r6x0](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/main/.agents/pm/issues/pm-context-r6x0.toon)

Discovered during: [pm-context-5njx](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/main/.agents/pm/chores/pm-context-5njx.toon)

> **@unbraind** (2026-08-08T22:24:45Z)
>
> Closing as **not a defect** — verified against the full reachable object graph, not just `main`.
> 
> The complete identity inventory for this repository is:
> 
> ```
> 1153461+unbraind@users.noreply.github.com
> 41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com
> 49699333+dependabot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com
> noreply@github.com
> <redacted-email>
> ```
> 
> Every one of these is an approved public identity. `<redacted-email>` in particular is the
> maintainer's **intentional public authoring identity** for the `unbraind/pm-*` fleet — it is
> published deliberately, and it is explicitly approved in the fleet's identity allowlist, which
> already documents exactly this distinction:
> 
> > The maintainer's public authoring address is an intentional public identity used across the
> > `unbraind/pm-*` fleet; it is approved here as a deliberate public authoring identity, not as
> > a blanket allowlist of personal addresses.
> 
> (see `.github/approved-git-identities.txt` in `unbraind/pm-vcs`, `unbraind/pm-rl`, `unbraind/pm-rust`)
> 
> So there is nothing to remediate, and **no history rewrite is authorized or needed** here.
> 
> ### Why this issue was fileable at all — the real gap
> 
> This is the third time an audit has been reported against this identity across the fleet
> (previously `pm-vcs-mhbz` and `pm-rust-6q0n`, both also closed as false). The common cause is
> that the identity allowlist and its audit exist in only **2 of 21** fleet repositories
> (`pm-vcs`, `pm-rl`; `pm-rust` carries the allowlist with a native audit). In the other 19 —
> including this one — an identity inventory turns up real addresses with **no allowlist to
> resolve them against**, so a correct-looking "non-allowlisted identity" finding is the
> inevitable result.
> 
> The actionable follow-up is therefore not a rewrite but a gate: port
> `scripts/audit-git-identities.ts` + `.github/approved-git-identities.txt` into the remaining
> fleet repositories so the approved identities are declared where the audit can see them.
> Tracked in the companion repository; this issue is closed in favour of that work.
Remove non-allowlisted personal identity from public git history
